title: LLM-Barber: Block-Aware Rebuilder for Sparsity Mask in One-Shot for Large Language Models
problem: LLM pruning generates irregular sparsity patterns that are difficult to exploit efficiently on hardware; post-hoc sparsity mask restructuring is needed to enable block-sparse execution.
motivation: Structured sparsity (block-wise pruning) enables efficient accelerator implementation; one-shot mask rebuilding eliminates fine-tuning overhead and maintains accuracy.
method: After pruning an LLM, zeros scatter randomly through the weight matrix, but hardware accelerators run fastest when zeros are grouped into blocks. LLM-Barber identifies the most important remaining weights by their magnitude, then restructures the pruning pattern to create contiguous blocks of zeros matching the accelerator's block size. It does this in one pass without retraining, reorganizing which weights get removed to optimize the sparsity mask for hardware execution.
key_novelty: Restructuring a pruned LLM's sparsity pattern into blocks—grouped zeros that hardware can execute efficiently—in one pass without retraining.
contributions: Weight importance analysis for structured pruning
Demonstrated efficiency gains on accelerator hardware
limitations: Analysis limited to abstract; specific LLM models and accuracy-efficiency trade-offs not detailed.
primary_theme: block-aware sparsity mask rebuilding for LLM acceleration
